doc: CutsceneSequencer tuning (M2-FP-01; docs/kb/tech/cutscenes.md). Times in seconds, distances in metres, sizes as a fraction of the screen height. music_stand_ins maps a cue's track id to an existing file under music_dir until Audio ships the real cue (placeholders for the first playable; nobody has approved them as final). vfx rows give the placeholder mote look per @vfx effect (colours from docs/kb/tech/glimmer.md). skip_hold_sec: how long ui_cancel is held to skip (a skip fast-forwards to the next choice or the end); skip_prompt: the 'hold to skip' fill, bottom right. face_poses: actor id -> a face-poses JSON (emotion -> blend shape weights; Character's file, read only) used by @face and by each line's [emotion]. lip_flap: blend shape weights held while DialogueBox reports the mouth open (the fallback for a rig without the viseme shapes). clips: the AnimationPlayer clip played per role (idle, talk, walk, run) when the actor's rig has it. key_light (M2-FP-10; cutscenes.md 'Key light'): on dialogue and portrait framing (a shot whose frame is at most close_half_frame_m tall above and below its aim) the cast is lit by a short-range copy of the zone sun instead of the sun itself: render layer `layer` holds the cast meshes while it is on (19: layer 20 is UndertowHalfRes.BODY_LAYER, which the main camera culls), and the shadow values follow character_shading.md 'Shadows on characters'. blink (M2-FP-18): every face rig closes the `shapes` (pose keys; a pair name drives both sides) to `weight` every interval_s (a seeded range per actor), over close_s, holds hold_s and opens over open_s; on_emotion_change adds a blink when a line or @face changes the expression. Lip sync (M2-CHR-10, replacing M2-FP-18's visemes block): game/data/cutscene/lipsync.json; a rig missing any of its viseme shapes keeps lip_flap.
_motion_note: M2-FP-29 (the human's playtest: turns snapped, walks started and stopped at once; game/cutscene/cutscene_motion.gd): a turn eases in and out on Godot's ease() curve turn_ease (negative = in-out) over turn_min_sec (no angle) up to turn_sec (a half turn; M2-HER-1113: 0.9, so the in-out ease peaks near 400 deg/s like a hero's field turn, where 0.45 peaked near 800 and read as a whip); a walk waits walk_anticipation_sec, speeds up over walk_accel_sec and slows over walk_decel_sec (both shortened together on a short walk); every clip change cross-fades over clip_blend_sec; a stand-in clip mark is glided onto over standin_glide_sec, unless it is farther than standin_cut_m: then it is a cut (M2-HER-1113: Ch9's pole_out mark is 30 m out on the harbour, and a glide there crossed it at 120 m/s).
_group_note: M4-CIN-1302: @anim <group> <clip> with no actor of that id plays on every actor named <group>_*, each after its own fixed delay of up to group_spread_sec (from its name), so a crowd turns as many people (act2_ch10.md T04, the clutch).
_ease_note: M2-FP-102 (the human's playtest: abrupt fades): @fade and the letterbox ease in and out on Godot's ease() curve (negative = in-out) instead of a linear ramp.
_hold_note: M2-FP-103 (the playtest: a kneeling Asha stood up for her first line): an @anim of one of hold_clips is a pose the actor holds (a hero body's play_clip hold) until its own next @anim or @mark, and its lines don't play the talk or idle clip over it. Any other @anim is a gesture, after which lines play talk and idle again.
_stand_in_note: M2-FP-103: clip_stand_ins maps '<actor>/<clip>' to a clip the rig has, played while the requested clip (assets_src/characters/requested_clips.json) is not built yet; the real clip plays as soon as the rig carries it. Rhen lies in the shallows as his KO pose (the human's playtest: his kneel twinned Asha's), sits up into his kneel and stands as his rise.

camera_breath.doc: M2-FP-104: a landed scripted shot turns by a slow sum of sines (yaw_deg / pitch_deg amplitude, averaged over the periods), easing in over ramp_sec; a cut or blend resets it. Deterministic.

sefir._note: M3-CIN-01: his tell (act1_npcs.md §1.6): a slow blink, one every 10-14 s; a changed expression is no reason for him to blink
